bibliographic.title: Compliance Generation for Privacy Documents under GDPR: A Roadmap for Implementing Automation and Machine Learning
bibliographic.authors: David Restrepo Amariles, Aurore Clément Troussel, Rajaa El Hamdani
bibliographic.venue: JURIX 2019 Workshop 'GDPR Compliance - Theories, Techniques, Tools', Universidad Politécnica de Madrid
bibliographic.citation_apa: Restrepo Amariles, D., Troussel, A. C., & El Hamdani, R. (2019). Compliance generation for privacy documents under GDPR: A roadmap for implementing automation and machine learning. arXiv:2012.12718.

methodology.method_family: Literature survey and roadmap/framework development (Privatech project)
methodology.study_design: Survey of GDPR automation research combined with analysis of corporate operational challenges and a compliance-generation roadmap
methodology.sample_description: Survey of existing research on GDPR automation and discussion of corporate/law-firm compliance practices; references Privatech prototype development
methodology.sector: Data protection compliance; corporations and law firms
methodology.technology_context: Machine learning, NLP classifiers, and automation tools for assessing and generating GDPR-compliant privacy documents

eligibility.exclusion_reason: Paper addresses GDPR compliance automation via ML/NLP for privacy documents but does not study conversational systems, chatbots, agents, or LLM-based generative AI governance.
eligibility.decision_rationale: Strong fit for accountability, compliance, and regulated privacy contexts, but outside the review's core focus on conversational governance in LLM-based systems. Useful as foundational/contextual background on corporate compliance automation and accountability documentation.
eligibility.manual_spotcheck_reason: Scope mismatch (no conversational AI, no LLMs) is explicit in the provided text.

appraisal.notes: Conceptual survey/roadmap with referenced prototype work; limited primary empirical reporting in the provided excerpts. Appropriate for framing compliance automation but not for evaluating conversational LLM governance mechanisms.

cerqual.explanation: Internally coherent roadmap for GDPR document compliance automation, but methodological detail on sampling, evaluation, and limitations is limited in the provided text. Relevance to the review's conversational-LLM governance focus is low despite strong regulatory-compliance relevance.

coding.theme: Automated GDPR compliance for privacy documents
coding.subtheme: ML/NLP roadmap for corporate and law-firm compliance
rq_alignment: accountability and compliance in regulated contexts

synthesis.main_claim: The paper proposes a roadmap to bridge GDPR automation research and corporate operational challenges by decomposing compliance issues into ML- and automation-addressable tasks for assessing and generating privacy documents.
synthesis.contribution: Shifts compliance research focus from consumer-centric and regulator-centric approaches to corporations and law firms as agents of compliance, and outlines the Privatech project for GDPR privacy-document assessment.
synthesis.limitations: Provided text does not detail systematic review methods, empirical validation, or study limitations; technology discussed is pre-LLM ML/NLP rather than generative LLMs; no conversational-system governance is addressed.
synthesis.use_in_review: Include as foundational/contextual evidence on accountability, GDPR compliance automation, and corporate privacy-document governance; exclude from central conversational-LLM governance synthesis.

evidence.claim: Paper focuses on corporate/law-firm GDPR compliance automation rather than consumer/regulator approaches.
evidence.excerpt: We shift this perspective with the Privatech project to focus on corporations and law firms as agents of compliance.

evidence.claim: Accountability and documentation of compliance are central requirements.
evidence.excerpt: data processors must implement accountability measures to assess and document compliance in relation to both privacy documents and privacy practices.

evidence.claim: Study design is a survey plus roadmap for ML/automation tasks.
evidence.excerpt: We survey, on the one hand, current research on GDPR automation, and on the other hand, the operational challenges corporations face to comply with GDPR

evidence.claim: Technology context is ML and automation, not LLMs or conversational systems.
evidence.excerpt: breaking them down into tasks that can be addressed through machine learning and automation

evidence.claim: Regulated-domain focus is GDPR and related privacy law.
evidence.excerpt: The adoption of the principle of accountability by recent regulations such as GDPR and CCPA

evidence.claim: NLP is used for privacy-policy analysis, not conversational governance.
evidence.excerpt: used ML and natural language processing (NLP) to automate vagueness assessment.

evidence.claim: Human annotation remains part of proposed automated assessment approaches.
evidence.excerpt: The most recent research underlines the need for a combination of crowdsourcing, ML, and NLP to analyze privacy policies at a large scale.

evidence.claim: Transparency in data practices affects user willingness to share data.
evidence.excerpt: The results reveal a correlation between transparency in data practices and the users' willingness to share data.

evidence.claim: Privatech tool supports assessment of privacy-document GDPR compatibility.
evidence.excerpt: We designed a tool under the name of Privatech, which seeks to assist in the assessment of the compatibility of privacy documents of companies with GDPR

evidence.claim: No conversational AI or LLM governance is discussed in the provided text.
